deep.reconstruction:
Context: Riemann is excerpting H. Hammer's German summary (Dingler's Polytechnisches Journal CXXV) of M. H. Jacobi's theory of electromagnetic motors (Bull. St. Petersbourg IX). The notation continues from the previous page: k is the emf of one cell, n the number of cells, ϱ the total resistance, β the number of windings, κ (transcribed 'x') a coefficient measuring coercive force, and v the machine speed. Primed quantities refer to the running machine.

Step 1 (implicit, mine). The counter-current is i1 = i - i' = κβ² i' v/ϱ. With i = nk/ϱ this gives i'(ϱ + κβ²v) = nk, so i' = nk/(ϱ + κβ²v).

Step 2 (eq. 11, misread as '4)'). The magnetic state while running is m' = β i' = βnk/(ϱ + κβ²v).

Step 3 (eq. 13). At uniform speed the mean mechanical resistance must equal the mutual attraction: R = μ' = m'^2.

Step 4 (eq. 18). Since √R = βnk/(ϱ + κβ²v), we get v = (βnk/√R - ϱ)/(κβ²). The useful work is therefore
T = Rv = (βnk√R - Rϱ)/(κβ²) = v(βnk)²/(ϱ + κβ²v)².

Step 5 (eqs. 20-21). Maximise in s = √R: the derivative of βnk·s - ϱs² vanishes at s = βnk/(2ϱ). Hence
- R0 = β²n²k²/(4ϱ²), which is μ/4;
- T0 = n²k²/(4ϱκ).

Step 6 (implicit, mine). At the optimum ϱ + κβ²v0 = 2ϱ, so v0 = ϱ/(κβ²) and i0' = i/2. Riemann's remark is therefore correct: changing β alters R0 and v0 but not T0.

Step 7 (eq. 26). Zinc consumed is q0' = n i0' = n²k/(2ϱ). The economic effect ('duty') is ε = T0/q0' = k/(2κ), independent of n and ϱ.

Rest of the page: two reading notes without mathematics.
- A note headed 'Siemens', reporting John Wilson's (Birmingham) calorimetric pyrometer. A platinum piece is heated, dropped into water, and the water's temperature rise is read on a mercury thermometer. Melting points are listed: silver 1890°F, copper 2220°, grey cast iron 2320°, wrought iron 3128°, Mondglas 2244°, crystal glass 2145°, copper slag 2046°. Stourbridge clay can replace platinum.
- An excerpt from Erdmann's Journal f. prakt. Chemie 58 of Pasteur (Comptes rendus 35, p. 176) on crystal form, composition and optical rotation. Optically active substances usually show non-superposable hemihedry. Some salts crystallise holohedrally from water but hemihedrally from nitric acid or other solvents: calcium bitartrate, ammonium bitartrate, and tartramide.
errors: No mathematical errors. All formulas (i', m', R, T in both forms, R0, T0, q0', ε) check out.
Minor: the derivation of i' from i1 = κβ²i'v/ϱ and the value v0 = ϱ/(κβ²) are left implicit.
The page states the maximum as a function of R rather than v; this is equivalent (v0 = ϱ/(κβ²)).

results.what: Current in a running motor reduced by back-emf: i' = nk/(ϱ + κβ²v)
results.modern_name: Back-EMF in DC motor circuit (Ohm's law with counter-emf)

results.what: Maximum mechanical power T0 = n²k²/(4ϱκ), reached when the current is half the stalled current
results.modern_name: Jacobi's law / maximum power transfer theorem

results.what: Duty (work per zinc consumed) at maximum power ε = k/(2κ), i.e. 50% efficiency
Wilson's calorimetric (method-of-mixtures) pyrometer and melting points
Pasteur on hemihedrism and optical activity, solvent-dependent hemihedry

deep.surprise_reason: These are reading notes excerpting Jacobi's published motor theory and summaries from chemistry and physics journals. Riemann adds no original mathematics; the content is the well-known Jacobi maximum-power result.
